# References · Mark I · Box of Scraps

> Systems programming and numerics: the memory hierarchy, floating point, integrators, allocators and Unix processes.

10 works · difficulty: ★☆☆ accessible · ★★☆ technical · ★★★ research-grade  
Read with the [three-pass method](../../docs/papers.md#how-to-read-a-paper). Every link is a Google Scholar search for the exact title. [Master index →](../../docs/papers.md)

## Start here

#### ★☆☆ Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd ed.)

Bryant & O'Hallaron · 2015 · *Pearson* · book · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Computer%20Systems%3A%20A%20Programmer%27s%20Perspective%20%283rd%20ed.%29%22)

- **Why:** The spine of Mark I: data, caches, processes, virtual memory and `malloc`, all from the programmer's side.
- **Read:** Ch. 6, 8, 9 and 10.

#### ★★☆ What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory

Ulrich Drepper · 2007 · *Red Hat technical report* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22What%20Every%20Programmer%20Should%20Know%20About%20Memory%22)

- **Why:** Everything about caches, TLBs and NUMA that a performance engineer needs.
- **Read:** §3 (CPU caches) and §6 (what programmers can do).

#### ★★☆ What every computer scientist should know about floating-point arithmetic

David Goldberg · 1991 · *ACM Computing Surveys* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22What%20every%20computer%20scientist%20should%20know%20about%20floating-point%20arithmetic%22)

- **Why:** The classic on IEEE 754, rounding and cancellation. Read it before writing LU.
- **Read:** §1–2; skim the proofs.

## Landmarks

#### ★☆☆ The UNIX time-sharing system

Ritchie & Thompson · 1974 · *Communications of the ACM* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22The%20UNIX%20time-sharing%20system%22)

- **Why:** The paper that introduced Unix: processes, files, pipes and the shell, in 11 pages.
- **Read:** All of it.

#### ★★★ The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 1: Fundamental Algorithms (3rd ed.)

Donald Knuth · 1997 · *Addison-Wesley* · book · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22The%20Art%20of%20Computer%20Programming%2C%20Vol.%201%3A%20Fundamental%20Algorithms%20%283rd%20ed.%29%22)

- **Why:** Boundary tags and the first-fit/best-fit analysis that every allocator still uses.
- **Read:** §2.5 (dynamic storage allocation).

#### ★★☆ Computer "experiments" on classical fluids. I. Thermodynamical properties of Lennard-Jones molecules

Loup Verlet · 1967 · *Physical Review* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Computer%20%22experiments%22%20on%20classical%20fluids.%20I.%20Thermodynamical%20properties%20of%20Lennard-Jones%20molecules%22)

- **Why:** The integrator you implement in `02-sim`, introduced for molecular dynamics.
- **Read:** The section on the integration scheme.

## Go deeper

#### ★★★ Anatomy of high-performance matrix multiplication

Goto & van de Geijn · 2008 · *ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Anatomy%20of%20high-performance%20matrix%20multiplication%22)

- **Why:** How BLAS actually reaches peak: packing, register blocking and the cache hierarchy.
- **Read:** All of it, after `make bench`.

#### ★★☆ Dynamic storage allocation: A survey and critical review

Wilson, Johnstone, Neely & Boles · 1995 · *International Workshop on Memory Management* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Dynamic%20storage%20allocation%3A%20A%20survey%20and%20critical%20review%22)

- **Why:** The allocator survey: policies, fragmentation, and why intuition is often wrong.
- **Read:** §1–3.

#### ★★★ Geometric numerical integration illustrated by the Störmer–Verlet method

Hairer, Lubich & Wanner · 2003 · *Acta Numerica* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Geometric%20numerical%20integration%20illustrated%20by%20the%20St%C3%B6rmer%E2%80%93Verlet%20method%22)

- **Why:** Why symplectic integrators conserve energy: the backward error analysis behind manual 03.
- **Read:** §1–5.

#### ★★☆ A fork() in the road

Baumann, Appavoo, Krieger & Roscoe · 2019 · *HotOS* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22A%20fork%28%29%20in%20the%20road%22)

- **Why:** A modern critique of `fork()`. Read it after you've built a shell around it.
- **Read:** All of it.
